title: AI inference startup Fal doubles its valuation to $16B as demand surges
slides: Why did Fal's valuation double to $16B so fast?
Demand for AI inference is surging beyond expectations
But inference margins are thinner than training
Your AI app costs may not drop as hoped
Test your inference provider's real latency today
thread_text:
1. Fal's $16B shock

Demand for AI inference is surging beyond what anyone predicted, and Fal just doubled its valuation to $16B. That speed hides a margin problem most builders haven't priced in.

2. Inference margins are thin

Serving models costs more per token than training them, because you pay for compute, latency, and reliability on every single request. Training is a one-time bill; inference is a meter that never stops.

3. Your app costs won't fall

Cheaper inference per token doesn't mean a cheaper product, because users send more requests as prices drop. Your bill can climb even when unit costs shrink.

4. Latency is the real test

Providers advertise average speeds, but your users feel the slow tail, not the mean. Measuring that gap is the only way to know what your app actually delivers.

5. Test your provider today

Run a real prompt through your live app and time the slowest response, not the fastest. If your provider can't show that number, you're guessing.
